terms.definition: The motion an object carries, computed as mass × velocity.
terms.function: Banks how hard an object is to stop and in which direction its motion is headed.
terms.whereItIs: Read on each cart's badge as kg·m/s.
terms.whyItMatters: It is conserved in collisions and explains crashes, rockets, and every moving disaster.

terms.definition: Momentum treated with its direction — pointing the way the object moves.
terms.whyItMatters: Left-momentum and right-momentum cancel like vectors, which is the whole trick behind conservation.
terms.whereItIs: On the arrows above each cart.

terms.definition: The rule that total momentum stays the same before and after an interaction.
terms.whyItMatters: Nothing creates or destroys momentum — the carts only swap it, which the banner proves.
terms.whereItIs: The floating-rect total that never changes.

terms.definition: A force applied over time (F × Δt) — the thing that changes momentum.
terms.whyItMatters: Longer crash time means smaller force for the same stop — that's why crumple zones save lives.
terms.where: The collision contact connecting the two carts.
